raw_response:
Ai, let me think about this year. Six mu isn't much land — just me and my wife working it mostly, our son works in the city and comes back at harvest to help. Thirty years I've been farming this ground. Every year pretty much the same: wheat in the fall, then maize after the wheat comes off in June. That's how everyone does it here in our village.

For the wheat, I'll plant around middle of October like always, once the maize is cleared off. I buy seed at the supply shop in town — the kind old Zhang next door uses, because his fields look good every year. Before I sow I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's what my father did and what I do. Then when the wheat greens up in the spring, around March, if it looks a bit yellow or thin I put down some urea on top, maybe half a bag per mu. I water three times usually — once before the ground freezes in November so it goes into winter with wet roots, once at green-up, and once when it's heading out in April. If May is dry I might water one more time for the grain to fill. Every time I turn on that well pump though, I'm counting the electricity. Six mu of watering isn't cheap.

Wheat harvest is early June. The combine comes through the village, I pay by the mu. Then I have maybe a week — sometimes less — to get the maize in. No time to plow. My cousin has a no-till planter, he does mine for a little money and I help him with something in return. I plant the hybrid maize seed, it's expensive, thirty-some yuan for a bag, but the yield is much better than the old kind, everyone uses hybrid now. I put compound fertilizer down with the seed, and when the maize is about knee-high in July I topdress some urea. Usually the summer rains do most of the watering for the maize, but if July turns dry I'll water once.

Pesticide — I spray the wheat once in spring for weeds, and if I see aphids coming I spray again. Maize I watch for borers. If I see them chewing I spray, otherwise I don't bother spending the money.

For yield, I expect about what I always get — maybe 400 kg of wheat per mu, 450 kg of maize. Some years more, some less, depends on the sky. Last year was alright, not bad. We keep some wheat flour for ourselves — my wife makes the mantou and noodles — and sell the rest. Maize mostly gets sold to the feed buyer who comes around.

Total money out of pocket for the year, I figure around six hundred yuan per mu across both crops, so around three thousand six hundred yuan for the six mu. That's a lot for us. I don't take chances with things I haven't tried.
